finding.title: Rewrite account_picker_an4_test.dart to exercise AccountPickerScreen's real sort/tap-guard code instead of a hand-copied replica
finding.rule: TQ-8 (regression test must pin the actual fix) / Feathers seam

evidence.quote:
// Test strategy: we test the ordering logic in isolation using the same sort
// algorithm as the fix, and verify the _switching guard behavior via a minimal

finding.why: The file never imports account_picker_screen.dart. AN-4 fixed two real bugs (unstable account ordering; no re-entrancy guard on rapid double-tap causing concurrent account switches — a genuine data-integrity risk for a local-first synced app). This test file instead hand-copies the sort comparator into `_sortedAccountDbFileNames` and hand-copies the `_switching` guard into `_TapGuardWidget`, then tests its own copies. If a future change to the real `_AccountTile._switching` guard or the real sort in AccountPickerScreen.build reintroduces either bug, this suite keeps passing because it never touches the production code — the regression protection is illusory.
finding.recommendation: Test the real AccountPickerScreen (as account_picker_screen_l1_test.dart and account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart in this same batch correctly do): drive the ordering assertion by seeding accounts via the registry and pumping the real screen (asserting tile order), and drive the tap-guard assertion by tapping the real _AccountTile through the pumped widget tree with a slow-resolving fake switch action.
acceptance_criteria: account_picker_an4_test.dart imports and pumps the real AccountPickerScreen (no private replica of the sort comparator or the _switching guard).
Reverting the AN-4 fix in account_picker_screen.dart (either the sort or the guard) makes this test fail red.

finding.title: Replace sign_in_context_reset_test.dart's source-text-matching 'wiring' assertions with real call-chain verification
finding.why: The 'wiring' group (4 tests) reads sign_in_controller.dart / account_picker_screen.dart as raw text with File.readAsStringSync() and asserts substring presence (e.g. 'routerProvider).pinGuard.lock()' appears somewhere after another substring). This proves the token exists in the file — including inside a comment, a dead branch, or an `if (false)` — not that the reset actually runs during a real sign-in. A refactor that renames a local variable, extracts the same call into a helper, or reorders it outside the funnel would either false-fail (token literally moved) or false-pass (token still present but now unreachable) without any real Riverpod/router state ever being observed. The file's own 'runtime semantics' group shows the better pattern is available (it drives the real PinGuard/activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider primitives directly) — it just never chains them through an actual signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle call.
finding.recommendation: Replace the source-grep assertions with an end-to-end check: seed a tutored selection + authenticated PIN scope, drive SignInController.signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle (as sign_in_controller_test.dart and the sign_in_*_throws_test.dart files in this batch already do with a stub router), and assert the real providers were cleared afterward — the same technique the 'runtime semantics' group in this file already uses for the primitives themselves.
acceptance_criteria: No test in this file reads a .dart source file as text to assert behavior.
Commenting out (not deleting) the _resetSessionContextForFreshSignIn() call inside _navigateAfterSignIn makes the corresponding test fail red.

finding.title: Add try/catch around onSendAgain/onVerified in EmailVerificationConfirmPanel and un-skip the C6/E5 regression tests
finding.rule: EH-2/EH-3 (typed exceptions handled at the boundary; no log-less catch) discovered via disclosed-but-unfixed test skips

evidence.quote:
// BUG: _wrapSendAgain uses try/finally but not try/catch, so exceptions
      // from onSendAgain propagate as unhandled async errors, crashing the

finding.why: `_wrapSendAgain`/`_wrapVerified` use try/finally with no catch, so any exception from the injected callback propagates as an unhandled async error instead of a graceful error state. The onVerified callback built in sign_in_controller.dart's buildVerificationCallback calls _refreshAndCheckVerified -> authRepo.reloadCurrentUser() with no surrounding try/catch, so a transient network error while the user is mid email-verification is a real, reachable path to this unhandled exception -- not just a theoretical one. Both regression tests that would catch this (C6, E5) are disclosed but left skip:true with no Linear id, so the gap is invisible to anyone not reading test source.
finding.recommendation: Add a catch clause to both wrapper methods that resets the loading flag and surfaces the failure (e.g. via a callback/snackbar, matching the pattern already used for signOut() failures elsewhere in this feature), then remove skip: true from C6 and E5.
acceptance_criteria: _wrapSendAgain and _wrapVerified catch and handle exceptions from the injected callbacks (no bare try/finally).
C6 and E5 in email_verification_confirm_panel_test.dart run (skip: true removed) and pass.

finding.title: Add ref.mounted guards to SignInController's post-await state writes and a dispose-mid-flight regression test
finding.rule: SM-4 (check ref.mounted after await in a Notifier before touching ref/state)
finding.why: signInControllerProvider is autoDispose and its methods await many things (registry lookups, Firestore fetches, SharedPreferences, sync-orchestrator pulls with 8s timeouts) with zero `ref.mounted` checks anywhere in the ~1000-line file, then keep calling `_ref.read(...)` / `state = ...` afterward. If the user navigates away (dialog dismissed, screen popped) while a sign-in is in flight, the provider can be disposed mid-await and the next `state = ...` throws Riverpod 3's UnmountedRefException in the app's most security-critical flow. None of the 5 sign-in notifier tests in this batch dispose the container between an await and the following state mutation, so this path is completely unexercised. (This gap is systemic — only 3 of ~32 autoDispose notifiers in lib/features use ref.mounted at all — so the fix likely belongs to a broader SM-4 sweep; flagged here specifically because this batch's test suite is the one place positioned to catch it for the highest-stakes notifier.)
finding.recommendation: Add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` (or equivalent) after each await inside signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle/_navigateAfterSignIn/etc. before the next state or ref.read, and add a test that disposes the container mid-flight (e.g. between two awaits in a stubbed slow authRepo call) and asserts no unhandled exception surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: A test that disposes the ProviderContainer while signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle is suspended on an await passes without an uncaught UnmountedRefException.
sign_in_controller.dart checks ref.mounted (or ref is otherwise guarded) after every await that is followed by a state or ref.read/ref.invalidate call.
